what: Encode of the decoded twitter.cbor through ref_binding with sharedrefs::on. Arm A: main 31ef9c9 with two changes (the write pass looks only at identities seen twice; the count pass encodes no leaves), seen a std::unordered_map. Arm B: A with seen a std::pmr::unordered_map on a std::pmr::monotonic_buffer_resource that lives one document. Time in microseconds per document, and the peak of heap bytes during one encode above the heap before it.
why: The owner asked for the numbers of the arena alone before deciding on it.
how: Time: Google Benchmark, one binary per arm, each built twice (a, b), 3 rounds alternating, --benchmark_min_time=0.1s --benchmark_repetitions=3, random interleaving, GLIBC_TUNABLES trim_threshold, mmap_threshold and top_pad high. Memory: one encode in a binary per arm that replaces the global operator new and delete, the aligned forms too, and counts malloc_usable_size; the writer has 1 MiB reserved before.
finding: Time: A 1438/1495, B 1271/1276, so the arena saves 13 percent. Peak heap during the encode: A 245 KiB, B 388 KiB, so the arena costs 143 KiB more at the peak (+58 percent), because freed nodes and old bucket arrays return only with the document.
